role: The AI brain of the app: it configures the Bedrock Claude models, assembles the CFO persona's system prompt from the user's financial data, defines the 43 tools the model can call in chat, and runs guard rails that validate and sanitise the model's output before it is saved.
detail: provider.ts wires three Bedrock models (Sonnet for chat, Haiku as utilityModel for classification/extraction, Opus reserved for "lifetime-once" archetype reveals), and context-builder.ts's buildSystemPrompt() fires 11 Supabase queries in parallel via Promise.allSettled, then assembles ~18 sections (persona, profile, financial snapshots, portrait, goals, balance sheet, country benchmarks, experiments, profiling) joined with '---'. Every chat tool follows the same factory pattern — createXTool(ctx) closing over {supabase, userId, conversationId, currency} — registered in tools/index.ts's createToolbox(); the persona's hard 'DO NOT CALCULATE' rule is enforced by dedicating tools like compute_goal_pace and compute_period_average to arithmetic the LLM is banned from doing. A distinct post-generation layer runs after streaming: insight-validator traces every number and merchant in prose back to a tool result, value-save-guard detects hallucinated 'saved it' claims made without a record_value_classifications call, persona-sanitiser regex-scans for voice leaks and rewrites dirty messages with Haiku before DB insert, and read-judge deterministically scores first Reads (250-word cap, exactly one CTA, no closing question). compose-first-read.ts is a separate one-shot orchestrator that generates the onboarding 'first Read' from pre-computed Layer 2/3/5 context with zero tool calls, while portrait-extraction.ts uses Haiku generateObject to mine completed conversations for behavioural traits written to financial_portrait.

keyFiles.why: 2752-line prompt assembler; buildSystemPrompt() runs 11 parallel Supabase queries and joins ~18 context sections
BASE_PERSONA derived from CFO-CONSTITUTION v1.4 — voice rules, arithmetic ban, the Gap protocol, [OPTIONS]/[CONFIRM_FACT] UI grammar
createToolbox(ctx) factory registering all 43 chat tools, each a closure over supabase/userId/conversationId/currency
Bedrock client + Sonnet/Haiku/Opus model routing from env vars, with cold-start model-ID logging for diagnosability
one-shot first-Read composer pulling Value Profile, cluster behaviour and goals — explicitly no tool calls during composition
runtime regex leak detector that rewrites off-voice messages with Haiku before they persist (and feed the prompt cache)

interestingFact: The runtime persona-sanitiser contradicts the persona it protects: BASE_PERSONA explicitly permits first person when it carries a real stance ("I'd push back on that" is given as a good example), yet persona-sanitiser.ts hard-bans \bI\b, \bI'd\b, \bme\b and \bmy\b, so any message using the constitution's own endorsed phrasing gets silently rewritten by Haiku before hitting the database — and the stated reason for scrubbing history is that persisted messages feed Bedrock's prompt cache, so one off-voice turn would otherwise get replayed into every subsequent prompt.

role: The deterministic number-crunching layer that turns raw transactions into monthly summaries, recurring-bill detections, behavioural features, and intent-vs-reality gap analyses that get injected into the AI's context — so the LLM never does the maths itself.
detail: Everything funnels through shared P&L predicates in categories.ts (isIncomeRow/isSpendRow/isNeutralCategory) so income, refunds, and transfer exclusions are computed identically by monthly-snapshot.ts (pure aggregateMonthSpending), spending-breakdown, and the pattern detectors. recurring-detector.ts gates candidates with coefficient-of-variation thresholds (MAX_AMOUNT_CV 0.20, MAX_GAP_CV 0.35, min 3 occurrences) to separate real bills from casual repeat spend. Two subfolders implement the "layered Read": cluster-behaviour/ (Layer 3) derives recurrence/trend/time-pattern/amount-profile/lifecycle per merchant or category with sample-size-scaled confidence, exposed to Claude via the get_cluster_behaviour tool; chat-signals/ (Layer 4) mines regret/enjoyment/context signals from chat messages using a regex pattern library first and a Haiku LLM fallback only when pattern confidence averages below 0.7. gap-analyser.ts (1188 lines) holds two full generations of the stated-intent-vs-actual-spending analysis — analyseGap (v1, five gap types like leaking_despite_awareness) and analyseGapV2 (three shapes: single_intent, multi_intent with per-time-slice breakdowns and a merchant-labelling learning state, and coverage_gap) — consumed by The Gap page, the analyse_gap chat tool, and the first-read composer.

keyFiles.why: 1188-line dual-generation gap engine (analyseGap v1 + analyseGapV2 shapes) powering The Gap page and chat tools
pure aggregateMonthSpending with careful refund/income/null-category bucketing rules, feeds monthly_snapshots
single source of truth for P&L classification predicates shared by every consumer
coefficient-of-variation regularity gate that decides what counts as a real recurring bill
pure Layer-3 derive functions (recurrence, trend, lifecycle) with confidence scaled by sample size
Layer-4 pipeline: regex patterns first, LLM fallback only under a 0.7 confidence threshold, writes chat_signals

interestingFact: The recurring-bill thresholds (MAX_AMOUNT_CV = 0.20, MAX_GAP_CV = 0.35) were tuned after a staging audit caught the detector classifying a user's trips to "Satans Coffee" and El Corte Inglés as weekly recurring bills — the comment in recurring-detector.ts preserves the incident, and the fix requires both consistent amounts AND consistent cadence, since habitual coffee runs repeat on schedule but vary in price.

role: The server-side HTTP layer of the app: 62 Next.js route handlers covering the streaming AI chat, bank-statement uploads, scheduled cron jobs, dashboard aggregations, onboarding insights, and account/data management.
detail: The centrepiece is chat/route.ts (1143 lines), which persists messages, builds a per-user system prompt via buildSystemPrompt(), streams Sonnet through the Vercel AI SDK's streamText with a Bedrock cachePoint on the system message, defines inline tools (update_user_profile with an ALLOWED_PROFILE_FIELDS allowlist and confidence thresholds, request_structured_input, update_value_category) plus the createToolbox() CFO tools, then runs deterministic post-stream validators (citation/projection/voice/chip checks, persona-leak sanitiser via Haiku) before saving the assistant message. Heavy async work rides on Next's after() — post-conversation portrait/profile extraction and chat-signal mining fire after the response, with daily crons (vercel.json schedules 8 of them, all gated by a CRON_SECRET bearer check and service-role Supabase clients) sweeping anything that failed. upload/route.ts is a multi-format import pipeline (CSV/screenshot/PDF/holdings) that chains categorisation, duplicate detection, snapshot refresh, recurring/holiday detection, nudge evaluators, and a merchant_aggregates RPC refresh. The insights routes compose and later delta-recompose the onboarding "First Read" into the same conversation once the Value Map populates Layer 2.

interestingFact: The chat route has a self-healing "hallucination guard": if the model's streamed reply claims it saved a value classification but never actually called record_value_classifications, the server detects it (detectValueSaveHallucination), then silently re-invokes Bedrock with toolChoice hard-locked to that one tool so the write actually lands — after the user has already seen the confident "saved it" text — logging value_save_hallucination_detected/recovered telemetry events. Bonus: the /api/tools/[tool]/route.ts documented in CLAUDE.md doesn't exist; all tool execution happens inline in the chat route.

role: The authenticated mobile-first "office" surface: a home screen of four accent-coloured folder cards (Goals, Cash Flow, Values, Net Worth) that open into per-folder dashboards, all wrapped in a persistent header + chat bar/sheet shell.
detail: The route-group layout (app/(office)/layout.tsx) is the real workhorse: it auth-gates via Supabase, loads office-only fonts (DM Sans, JetBrains Mono, Cormorant Garamond), enforces onboarding-step redirects (bouncing mid-flow "Marcus" users back to /onboarding-v2/*), and mounts ChatProvider/ChatBar/ChatSheet so the CFO chat overlays every office page. The home page (office/page.tsx) is a server component running eight parallel Supabase queries (provenance, gap analysis, archetype, assets/liabilities, events, profile, primary goal) that feed OfficeHomeClient, which composes four FolderSection cards — a reusable primitive that renders a floating folder tab tinted via CSS color-mix from a single folderColors token. Each folder's detail dashboard (e.g. CashFlowDashboard) is a client component pulling live data through SWR hooks (/api/dashboard/trends, /api/profile/income-shape) and rendering a serif "Briefing" narrative block, metric rows, trend bars and drill-down links. Subtitle copy for the home cards lives in folder-subtitles.ts, which encodes CFO Constitution voice rules in code (goal-aware phrasing like "€460 surplus this month · feeds your goal", no first person, real numbers only).

interestingFact: Every render of the office layout schedules a fire-and-forget goal recompute using Next.js's after() — and because cookies() is illegal inside after(), it deliberately swaps the RLS request client for a cookie-free service-role client scoped by userId, with a 30-minute staleness TTL so a whole browsing session only triggers one recompute. Also, each dashboard's narrative Briefing card is typeset in Cormorant Garamond and literally signed "— C." like a memo from the CFO.

role: Turns any bank statement file (CSV, XLSX, PDF, OFX, QIF, screenshot) into deduplicated, doubly-categorised transactions in the database — assigning each one both a traditional category (Groceries, Transport...) and a value category (Foundation/Burden/Investment/Leak).
detail: There are no per-bank parsers: parseFileOnClient (format-detect-client.ts) runs in the browser, hashes the sorted lowercased CSV headers (fingerprint.ts), and POSTs only that hash plus the first 5 rows to /api/detect-format, where Haiku infers a reusable FormatTemplate (column mapping, date/decimal/sign convention) that parseUniversalCSV then applies to the full file client-side; repairTemplate() sanity-checks the LLM's chosen amount column against real rows and swaps in the first numeric column if Haiku picked a narrative one. The server-side runImportPipeline (upload/pipeline.ts) then does three passes: deterministic categoriseByRules (five tiers — user merchant rules, raw-text P2P markers, recurring-expense inheritance, DB category examples, ~170 multilingual keyword rules with amount heuristics), a batched Haiku fallback (llmCategorise, max 50 descriptions per call) whose confident results are persisted to user_merchant_rules so the same merchant never needs an LLM again, and row-by-row inserts where Postgres 23505 unique-violations on a sha256 dedupe hash are counted as duplicates rather than errors (the partial unique index can't be targeted by Supabase's onConflict). Value categories are resolved in parallel via assignValueCategory/resolveValueCategory from the user's Value Map rules, and universal-csv.ts is the single choke point enforcing the debits-negative/credits-positive sign convention every downstream analytic assumes.

keyFiles.why: orchestrates the whole import: dedupe, rules pass, LLM pass, value categories, inserts, failure alerting
browser-side entry point routing CSV/XLSX/PDF/OFX/QIF to the right parser and the template API
template-driven parser replacing all per-bank parsers; enforces the global sign convention and repairs bad LLM templates

Haiku batch fallback that also writes learned user_merchant_rules so future imports skip the LLM

interestingFact: For CSV/XLSX uploads the full statement never leaves the browser — parsing is fully client-side, and the server only ever sees a SHA-256 of the alphabetically sorted headers plus the first 5 rows. Haiku infers a FormatTemplate from that sample once, it's cached keyed on the header hash, and every subsequent upload of the same bank layout (by any user) parses with zero LLM tokens; sorting the headers before hashing exists specifically because Revolut occasionally shuffles column order between export versions.

role: The card-sorting experience where users label transactions as Foundation/Investment/Burden/Leak, which the system turns into a money-personality archetype and a per-category "stated intent" profile the CFO uses in chat.
detail: Two UI surfaces share one library: `demo-flow.tsx` runs the anonymous pre-signup version on country-specific sample transactions (ending in an LLM-generated reading plus html2canvas share card in `demo-reveal.tsx`), while `value-map-flow.tsx` is a multi-mode state machine ('onboarding' | 'checkin' | 'personal') that can run on real transactions built from the First Read's hook candidates (`hook-transactions.ts`). Each sort is scored deterministically: `calculatePersonality` maps quadrant spend percentages to one of five archetypes via a priority cascade (leak ≥25% → Drifter, burden ≥30% → Anchor, investment ≥35% → Builder, foundation ≥50% → Fortress, else Truth Teller), and `buildUserValueProfile` aggregates rules (2x weight) plus user-confirmed transactions (1x) into per-category/per-merchant quadrant distributions — the Layer 2 input to the layered Read. `select-cards.ts` picks up to 10 retake cards by seeding the promised hook merchants, then adding merchants whose Layer-3 behavioural shape most likely contradicts stated intent (weighted divergence score: 0.4 spend, 0.25 trend, 0.15 frequency, 0.2 mean), and `regenerate-archetype.ts` re-derives the archetype via Bedrock Sonnet from accumulated retakes, corrections, and monthly snapshots.

interestingFact: The card UI covertly times the user's psychology: each card records first_tap_ms, card_time_ms, and deliberation_ms (the gap between first quadrant tap and confirm), the quadrant buttons are deliberately inert for a 1500ms GATE_DURATION so tap timings are meaningful, and an observation rules engine mines this telemetry for "hesitation spikes" and same-category contradictions. Meanwhile feedback.ts holds regex-keyed merchant snark ("Deliveroo at that hour — rarely a planned meal") under an explicit design rule in the comments: '"Good choice!" is never acceptable.'

role: Runs the value-first signup journey — struggle question, AI goal chat, statement upload, income/rent form, fixed-cost confirmation, and the composed "first Read" — as a deterministic state machine driven by the user_profiles.onboarding_step column.
detail: Each beat advances via a server action (submitStruggle, completeGoalBeat/skipGoalBeat, submitIncome/submitRent, confirmFixedCosts, and the generic advanceStep, which calls markOnboardingCompleteIfReady when the step hits first_read_delivered), and resumeRoute() in lib/onboarding-v2/resume.ts maps every step — including four generations of legacy stamps like essentials_done and archetype_shown — to the right screen so mid-flow users are never stranded. Notably, the code has moved past CLAUDE.md's description: the upload → essentials → confirm → Read beats no longer run on standalone pages but inside the office chat sheet via OnboardingBeatHost (keyed off IN_SHEET_BEAT_STEPS), with pages like /onboarding-v2/upload reduced to redirect-only shells. The only LLM-driven beat is the goal chat, which GoalBeatWatcher observes by polling /api/onboarding/essentials-status every 2.5s, routing onward when a goal lands or when a regex quickcheck (quickClassifyGoalDeferral) / 7-turn stall marks the user goal_chat_tentative — with a 4s grace so the CFO's streamed acknowledgement finishes before redirect. confirmFixedCosts commits the whole reconcile screen in one shot, routing user corrections differently by row origin (rent → user_profiles, declared → in-place update, detected → dismiss-and-redeclare as source='banked_edit' so the next detector run can't clobber the edit).

interestingFact: OnboardingBeatHost carries a war-story comment about a race it fixes: the old first-Read hand-off fired three Next.js navigations in one tick (a router.replace with ?chat=open, a router.refresh, and ChatOpenerTrigger's param-stripping replace), and Next coalesced the refresh away — so the force-dynamic office layout never re-rendered and users stared at an infinite loading spinner over a Read that was already composed and waiting. The fix loads the conversation directly into ChatProvider state (which lives above the host, surviving its unmount) and fires exactly one lone router.refresh().

role: The system-computed "proactive brain" of the CFO: it sends rule-based notification nudges on cron schedules, learns to predict how a user feels about each transaction from their corrections, keeps goal progress and pace numbers fresh, and derives net-worth traits from declared assets and debts.
detail: Nudges are fully declarative: NUDGE_RULES in rules.ts defines 10 nudge types with {{mustache}} templates, cooldown_hours, and max_per_month; per-type evaluators (e.g. evaluatePaydaySavings, which flags any credit within ±20% of stated net income in the last 3 days) are fanned out by three cron routes (nudges-daily/weekly/monthly), all funnelled through canSendNudge (prefs + cooldown + monthly cap) before createNudge inserts. Prediction is a correction-signal learning loop: learning-engine.ts computes weighted-majority merchant rules plus time-context and amount-band variants, then predictor.resolveValueCategory walks a 9-tier resolution order (merchant_time → merchant_amount → merchant → category_* → global → category_default → none) with per-tier confidence thresholds and a recency boost up to +0.05 decaying over 90 days, while backfill.ts re-scores unconfirmed transactions after rules change. Goals centralise one pace formula — computePaceAndOnTrack in pace.ts, shared by create_goal, plan_event, and recompute.ts (which sets current_amount = SUM(contributions) via a recompute_goal_current_amount SQL RPC and is TTL-gated to 30 minutes on office-layout render) — with investment goals paced via compound growth instead of flat division. Balance-sheet's updateAssetPortrait recomputes asset_profile traits (has_savings, net_worth_bracket, has_high_interest_debt, allocation summary) into financial_portrait after every asset/liability upsert, and ensureLiabilityForDebtGoal auto-seeds a liability row from a debt-clearance goal's name via regex type inference so payoff tools never re-ask for a balance the user already stated.

derives net-worth and debt traits into financial_portrait after every asset/liability write

interestingFact: The learning engine can decide that price, not merchant, is what the user actually cares about: computeAmountRules splits a merchant's correction signals at the median amount, and if the cheap half and expensive half have different dominant value categories (each with >= 0.65 agreement), it deletes the flat merchant rule entirely and replaces it with two merchant_amount rules whose boundary is the midpoint of the two straddling transaction amounts — so "a 4 EUR coffee at Starbucks is foundation but a 40 EUR order is a leak" is learned automatically from as few as 4 corrections.

role: The client-side chat experience — a bottom-sheet conversation with the CFO full of inline interactive widgets — plus the dual-view (Spending vs Values) financial dashboard, with the chat's shared text parsers and rate limiting in lib/chat.
detail: ChatProvider wraps @ai-sdk/react's useChat with a DefaultChatTransport to /api/chat, exposing a React context (startConversation, loadConversation, handleSend, sheet open/close) consumed by ChatSheet/ChatBar/ChatInput; eleven typed conversation kinds (first_read, monthly_review, chip_opener, etc.) auto-open by sending a hidden "[System: ...]" user message whose prompt text is hardcoded client-side. MessageList strips custom inline markers from assistant text — [OPTIONS] (tap chips), [STATS] (stat cards), [CTA:type], [CONFIRM_FACT] (yes/no tap) — via pure parsers in lib/chat, and maps AI SDK v5 "tool-{name}" message parts into rich widgets: StructuredInput forms, LabelTransactionsBlock quadrant labelling, ScenarioResult/TripPlanResult visualisations, and SavedItemCard receipts built by savedCardBuilders.ts. It also carries "wow plumbing": FirstInsightInstrumentation fires delivered/scrolled_to_bottom events on the first Read and registers it so handleSend can log substantive replies within a 5-minute window. DashboardClient toggles Spending vs Values views (persisted to localStorage), lazy-loads all four Recharts components (~200KB) with skeletons, and deep-links chart segments to the filtered /transactions page.

interestingFact: The client fakes system prompts through the user channel: ChatProvider sends user-role messages starting with "[System: ...]" to kick off typed conversations, and handleOptionSelect even regex-sniffs chip text like "let's do a few now" to inject a forced request_structured_input tool call — MessageList then hides every user message beginning with "[System:" so the user never sees the puppeteering. Relatedly, options-parser.ts explicitly codes around Claude "frequently forgetting" its closing [/OPTIONS] tag, including a fallback that promotes any trailing 2–4 short bullets into tap chips unless they look like money (/\d{2,}[.,]\d{2}/).

role: The database layer: 93 SQL migration files that define and evolve the Postgres schema (tables, row-level security, GDPR functions), plus three tiny Supabase client factories the rest of the app uses to talk to it.
detail: Migrations run 001_initial_schema through 072_demo_session_claim_guard, growing from ~10 core tables (user_profiles keyed to auth.users, transactions, conversations) to 45 tables covered by per-table RLS policies of the form "X_select_own ... using (user_id = auth.uid())"; ten separate "prod-backfill-*" files are manual, Lewis-only production scripts that are deliberately not part of the auto-applied sequence. GDPR lives in the schema itself: migration 028 adds deleted_at/anonymised_at to every user table and defines delete_user_account()/export_user_data() SQL functions (repaired in 070 after they broke when trips was renamed). src/lib/supabase has exactly three client factories — client.ts (createBrowserClient), server.ts (createServerClient over Next cookies(), imported by 92 files), and service.ts (service-role key that bypasses RLS, imported by 35 files, used for cron and system writes) — plus types.ts, a 2,889-line file generated from the live schema.

interestingFact: The migration numbering is knowingly broken and it doesn't matter: there is no 061 at all, while 045, 052, and 055 each exist twice with different names — safe because Supabase tracks migrations by timestamp version, not filename prefix. The history even contains migrations about migrations: 043 does no DDL whatsoever, it just INSERTs four missing rows into supabase_migrations.schema_migrations because prod's schema had the changes but its tracker didn't, and 048 exists purely to "repair onboarding_v2 columns on prod" — the drift between staging and production is written into the migration history itself.

role: Three layers of quality checks: ~90 vitest unit tests across src, a Playwright suite that walks 10 fake user personas through the real onboarding flow and grades the AI's "first Read" with an LLM judge, and a golden-set eval loop that keeps that judge calibrated against the founder's own taste.
detail: The persona runner (runPersona in persona-runner.ts) creates a real staging Supabase user, drives the browser through struggle → goal → upload → income/rent → confirm → first Read via playwright-driver.ts (which polls the DB for streamed assistant messages rather than scraping mid-stream, and fast-forwards the 90-second-gated goal beat via an admin client), then asserts DB invariants and scores each persona on three layers: functional, visual (screenshots), and LLM. The LLM layer in runner/judge.ts runs deterministic hard-rule pre-checks first — banned words/patterns, and a hallucination check that extracts currency-anchored money tokens and flags any figure above an "egregious floor" of 1.5x max(income, spend) not matching the persona's CSV — before Haiku scores Likert dimensions like warmth and accuracy. Separately, eval/ is a self-improving judge system: golden-set pairs of Read variants are hand-rated by Lewis via scripts/eval/rate.ts, judges are versioned TypeScript modules emitting a scalar wow_score in [0,1] (active one named in the CHAMPION pointer file), and candidate judges only get promoted if they beat the champion on both a train fold and a deterministic sha256-hashed holdout fold. Plain vitest units (npm test, vitest.config.ts, node environment) cover parsers, analytics, AI tools, and prompt composition throughout src.

role: The repo's institutional memory: a constitution defining the AI persona, a 2,900-line session log, dated audit snapshots, and decision records that every coding session is expected to read before touching code and update afterwards.
detail: Two audit layers coexist: repo-root audit/ holds a numbered phase pipeline (01-knip.md through 07-summary.md, raw tool output plus human-curated summaries) capped by audit-zero.md and audit-zero-killlist.md — the v2.6 "Audit Zero" that verified all 59 API routes live, sorted every dead-code candidate into DELETE / NEEDS-LEWIS / FALSE-POSITIVE with three-search evidence, and wrote guarded prod-backfill SQL that only the human owner (Lewis) may apply. CFO-CONSTITUTION.md (v1.5, 418 lines) is the canonical persona source — when a system prompt conflicts with it, the prompt is rewritten by re-derivation, never patched with corrective instructions. cfos-office/SESSION-LOG.md (56 entries) records each session's branch, Phase-0 findings (labelled D1, D2...), files touched, and lessons so the next session "can pick up cold"; CODE-MAP.md and BUILD-STATUS.md are point-in-time snapshots corrected via explicit "superseded by Audit Zero" annotations that preserve the disproven claims rather than silently editing them.

interestingFact: The read-only Audit Zero dead-code sweep accidentally found and fixed a live production outage: both GDPR SECURITY DEFINER SQL functions (delete_user_account and export_user_data) still referenced the dropped public.trips table, so account deletion and data export had been failing with error 42P01 for every production user — invisible to the audit's own tooling because the code sweep only scanned TypeScript .from() calls, never SQL function bodies, a gap the kill list now tracks as a follow-up for the three remaining SECURITY DEFINER functions.
